title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Cleric (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Cleric** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Faith-focused class, with decent Attunement, Strength, and Luck. This makes them well-suited to a Miracle-heavy build, and to using the many Lightning-attuned weapons as they are often also have good Strength-scaling.

While it does indeed have spells, in the form of Heal (which heals) and Force (which throws enemies away from you), it does not have any that causes damage, with the earliest ones not being found until Cathedral of the Deep or Farron Keep. This means the class will have to focus primarily on weapons initially, and will do well to keep them upgraded as offensive Miracles consume a lot of Focus Points.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Cleric (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : This is the only spellcasting-focused starting class in Dark Souls 3 that doesn't have a damage-boosting ring. Presumably this is because the Cleric doesn't have a damaging Miracle equipped from the start, and the Morne's Ring can instead be found in the Road of Sacrifices.
This class has remained remarkably similar throughout the series, always carrying a Mace and the Heal Miracle.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet: The Cleric's Sacred Chime is a fairly good casting tool and is actually the strongest casting tool for Miracles from 45 to 49 Faith. Its Spell Buff (the stat that affects how strong scaling spells are) doesn't actually increase until at least 19 Faith has been reached. Its Weapon Art is Gentle Prayer, a regenerative effect that always restores 360 hp over the course of a minute as long as the Chime is held in an active hand (so replacing it with another item stops it, as does two-handing the item in the other hand). This effect will actually outheal the Heal Miracle by up to 20% until the Chime's Spell Buff reaches 120, and even afterwards it is a strong if slow alternative due to only having about a third the cost in Focus Points.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Cleric Set is a light, caster-type armor set and as such has low physical defences and high elemental defences, while also having high Poison and Curse resistances.

The first trainer for more Miracles is found in the Undead Settlement for further development.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Mace is an unexpectedly strong weapon for what may at first seem like a spellcasting class, but in reality it is often a **Cleric's** main armament. This is because Strike damage is often the strongest physical damage type as armored and skeletal enemies are weak to it (most other physical damage types have fewer enemies weak to them), strong Strength-scaling for easy damage increases, a fairly good moveset, and has a good Weapon Art for trading hits with opponents. How the Weapon Art works is that Perseverance adds a flat 45% extra absorption and causes the attacks of light weapons to bounce off the user, while also granting great Hyper Armor to prevent being staggered.

The Blue Wooden Shield is not very good, having only decent physical and magic defence with serviceable Stability. While it does have Parry (albeit the inferior Medium Shield version), a strong Weapon Skill shield like the early Silver Eagle Kite Shield would probably serve as a better replacement.

title: Corvian Storyteller
snippet:
Corvian Storyteller -  Dark Souls III - enemy - description 
 description : Tall avian humanoids that act as shamans for the lesser Corvians. Storytellers use their staff's weapon art and a slow, short ranged wave of fire in combat and are capable of riling up their pack members to make them more aggressive. They are always accompanied by several Corvians.

title: Corvian Storyteller
snippet:
Corvian Storyteller -  Dark Souls III - enemy - notes 
 notes : Susceptible to Bleed, Poison and Toxic.
Susceptible to Rapport.
There are actually two screams that the storytellers use: one is quicker and quieter, and only alerts other corvians to your presence, but on most occasions it doesn't transform them: he uses this scream most often when you have been spotted but have not attacked yet. The second scream comes after he bends down, shakes, and then lets out a much louder scream: this is the scream that *always* transforms his lesser corvians and frenzies them in the process. This scream in particular is often used after he is attacked or he witnesses you killing a lesser corvian. If they are already transformed and he uses the second type of scream, the corvians with him will randomly attack the environment in their hysteria.
Unlike the lesser brethren, the storyteller cannot fly in short bursts, nor run. They can only walk slowly, and often just side to side.

title: Corvian Storyteller
snippet:
Corvian Storyteller -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Although physically imposing, Storytellers have little vitality and offer little in the way of physical offense. From a distance, they will use their staff's weapon art to prevent the player from reaching them, but there is a long delay before they can cast the spell and they are easily staggered out of it. They may also cast a wave of fire from the tip of their staff, in a semi-circular motion.

Storytellers will alert any nearby Corvians once they spot the player, which will cause them to begin transforming into their berserk state. It is recommended to eliminate this enemy swiftly before it can draw attention.

title: Corvian Storyteller
snippet:
Unlike the lesser brethren, the storyteller cannot fly in short bursts, nor run. They can only walk slowly, and often just side to side.

title: Hollowing
snippet:
Hollowing -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - reversing_hollowing 
 reversing_hollowing : The process of reversing Hollowing will remove all levels of Hollowing from the player. However, because they still possess Dark Sigils, they will resume Hollowing with each subsequent death, making the effect temporary. Thus, this "cure" is only cosmetic in nature, as well as losing access to the bonus Luck of Hollow-infused weapons.

Consumption of a Purging Stone will immediately remove all Hollowing. Purging Stones may be found as loot across Lothric, or purchased from Yuria of Londor for 4,500 souls.
Praying at either the Statue of Velka or the Purging Monument will present the option of "Request Dissolution," which will also remove all current levels of Hollowing at a cost of the player's Soul Level times 100. This option is cheaper than purchasing a Purging Stone so long as the player is below Soul Level 45.

title: Hollowing
snippet:
Hollowing -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - hollowing_cures 
 hollowing_cures : There are two different "cures" for Hollowing, one temporary and one permanent:

title: Hollowing
snippet:
Hollowing -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Hollowing** is a gameplay mechanic in *Dark Souls III*, which can be accessed by drawing out the player's "true strength" through Yoel of Londor.

title: Hollowing
snippet:
Hollowing -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - notes 
 notes : Equipping the Untrue Dark Ring will give the player the appearance of a human, regardless of Hollowing level, allowing the player to appear human and also retain access to the bonus Luck of Hollow-infused weapons. However, this comes at the cost of using up one of the player's four precious ring slots.
When entering a new NG+ cycle, all held Dark Sigils are removed, but Hollowing level is retained.

title: Hollowing
snippet:
Hollowing -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - healing_the_dark_sigil 
 healing_the_dark_sigil : The more permanent option for curing Hollowing is to obtain the Fire Keeper Soul and give it to the Fire Keeper. The player must then pay a soul cost equal to the amount of souls they would pay to level up from their current level, by a number of levels equal to the amount of Dark Sigils held. Thus, if the player is high level and has accepted the additional Dark Sigils from Anri of Astora's wedding, the price for healing the Dark Sigil can be extremely high.

Healing the Dark Sigil is permanent, as it will remove all held Dark Sigils and reset Hollowing to zero. Because of this, it will break the alliance with Yuria of Londor, as the Dark Sigils are required for obtaining the Usurpation of Fire ending.

title: Hollowing
snippet:
Hollowing -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - description 
 description : After recruiting Yoel at the Undead Settlement and sending him to Firelink Shrine, the player can accept his offer to draw the Ashen One's true strength out. Accepting this offer allows the player to level up at total of five times at no soul cost. Accepting a level from Yoel will grant the player with a Dark Sigil each time, which in turn affects the rate of Hollowing. Each subsequent level-up with Yoel will require a higher level of Hollowing before it can be accessed, meaning that the player must die a few times between each session.

title: Hollowing
snippet:
Hollowing -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - effects 
 effects : When the player has at least one Dark Sigil in their inventory, their Hollowing will increase with each death, by a multiple of the number of Dark Sigils carried. Once Hollowing reaches 15, the player will take on the appearance of a Hollow, just as in previous games, though the effect is purely cosmetic.

Additionally, at 15 Hollowing and beyond, the player unlocks the secondary effects of weapons infused with a Hollow Gem, gaining bonus Luck based on the upgrade level of the weapon.

title: Human Effigy

Human Effigy -  Dark Souls II - item - lead 
 lead : A **Human Effigy** is a restorative item and starting gift in *Dark Souls II*.

title: Human Effigy
snippet:
It takes 30 minutes for the burning of a Human Effigy to wear off, and once the duration has expired, the player will be able to be invaded by other players again, as well as summon friendly phantoms or dark spirits. This only applies to the area in which the effigy was burned, and the player must remain in that area for the effigy timer to count down; the player can end the effect prematurely by resting at the particular bonfire and selecting the "Nullify Human Effigy's Effect" option. Time spent outside the area will not reduce the timer, so it is advised to remain in the location for the duration of the effect if one does not wish to end it prematurely.

One Human Effigy must also be given to Darkdiver Grandahl for each attempt in the Dark Chasm of Old, until Darklurker is defeated.

title: Human Effigy
snippet:
Human Effigy -  Dark Souls II - item - player_versus_player 
 player_versus_player : Players receive one Human Effigy after successfully defeating another invading player; this counts for both NPC invaders and online invaders. Black Phantoms that do not have an invasion message, such as the one found above Mytha's fog gate, will not give Effigies, but instead drop a +5 variant of their gear.
Players will also receive a Human Effigy for defeating a player summoned into their world through the Red Sign Soapstone.

title: Human Effigy
snippet:
Human Effigy -  Dark Souls II - item - general_information 
 general_information : Restores the player back to human form, allowing their health bar to recover up to its maximum value and allowing the player to see and interact with summon signs.

Burning Human Effigies at bonfires temporarily decreases the player's world priority in the invasion selection process and disables the ability to summon other players except NPCs; this includes disabling the ability to use Cracked Blue Eye Orbs and Cracked Red Eye Orbs, but they can still place down their own summon sign to be summoned into other worlds. The effect allows players to perform various tasks in the location they burnt the effigy at, without having to worry about potential engagements by other players. This makes them ideal for when a player wishes to farm enemies for particular items, as well as preventing their summon signs from disappearing due to another player invading their world.

title: Human Effigy
snippet:
Human Effigy -  Dark Souls II - item - alternatives 
 alternatives : Effigies can be difficult to acquire, but they are not the only way to become human again. These things can also reverse Hollowing:
Being summoned as a phantom or shade will turn the player human upon successfully completing their duty.
The player can find a shrine down a short path found above the fourth bonfire in Shrine of Amana down a short path that will turn the player human for free. This method only works if the player has no effigies. Dropping the effigies on the ground to remove them from the player's inventory will not work.
A Ring of Life Protection or Ring of Soul Protection will prevent the player from Hollowing after dying as well as other benefits, and can be repaired for a respectable amount of Souls when they break upon death.

title: Irithyllian Slave
snippet:
Irithyllian Slave -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Irithyllian slaves are weak opponents physically; however, their threat comes from the difficulty in locating them. They will often hide in corners, underneath stairs and behind doors to ambush the player, so it is recommended to always mind one's surroundings when navigating the city. Their white eyes give away their location, although their thin form can make them challenging to hit with ranged weapons. As they are always found in packs, the player should progress slowly to avoid becoming surrounded.

Most slaves use claymores, although some can cast projectiles at a distance. They tend to be positioned behind other slaves in an attempt to goad the player toward them, and will flee to another location if pursued.

A few slaves in the basement behind the Church of Yorshka will crawl toward the player to attack them. They can also drop down from above, which leads to a damaging grab attack.

title: Katanas (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Katanas (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Katanas** are a weapon type in *Dark Souls III*. Katanas are characterized by their quick slashing and thrusting dashing attacks. Most are capable of strong sweeping slash attacks as well as thrusts. Many Katanas have a weapon skill that allows them to Parry or perform a sweeping slash. Additionally, all Katanas have a Bleed effect and will benefit from the Luck stat.

title: Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Knight Shield is, along with the Herald's Kite Shield, one of only two starting shields with 100% physical blocking, giving the Knight considerable extra survivability early on. However, its elemental defences are bad and it has somewhat mediocre Stability, making it easier to break that block. It has the Parry, allowing for critical hits if the user knows how to time it properly against enemies.

The Knight Set it is carrying is the strongest starting armor set, with quite good physical defenses and respectable elemental defences, and has a good amount of Poise for if using a weapon or attack capable of activating Hyper Armor. It does however have mediocre status resistances and is fairly heavy, and the Knight largely lacks the ability to exploit its Poise unless a larger weapon is acquired.

title: Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The adequate mental stats mean that just one point in either Intelligence or Faith could let it pick up some helpful spells, Soul Arrow, Spook, and Magic Weapon with the Sorcerer's Staff for the former and Heal Aid with the Talisman for the latter.

Its extremely low Luck of 7, shared with the Pyromancer class, means it is often optimal for a large amount of non-pyromancer, non-luck based builds, due to not wasting any of its starting point in that often sub-optimal stat, though it does lack other classes' starting equipment which might help make them initially more optimal/have earlier access to items for that role.

title: Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Knight (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Knight** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is the most newcomer friendly-class in Dark Souls 3, thanks to its strong and versatile weapon, its 100%-physical block shield, its strong armor, and its well-rounded stats. It is also suitable to a wide variety of builds thanks to its good Strength and Dexterity, and decent Intelligence and Faith. It also has good Vitality, letting it carry heavier equipment easier.

The Long Sword is a strong and versatile weapon, with fast swings on its light attacks and a strong thrusting attack as its one-handed heavy attack, capable of dealing heavy damage if a Counter Attack is landed. Its Weapon Art, Stance, is similarly versatile, as following as using a light attack while holding the stance leads to a block-breaking uppercut while the heavy attack version is a lunging thrust to catch enemies off guard.

title: Luck
snippet:
Luck -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Luck** is a stat in *Dark Souls III*. It determines the player's Item Discovery and the effectiveness with luck scaling weapons, such as the Man-grub's Staff, Anri's Straight Sword and Hollow-infused weapons, as well as increasing Bleed and Poison build-up.

Item Discovery determines the likelihood of an enemy dropping items. The higher it is, the easier it is to get drops.

Unlike other offensive stats, luck scaling is not displayed on the weapon's stat screen.

As with every other stat in the game, it also increases the player's defenses. As well, leveling Luck will increase the player's Curse resistance.

title: Man-grub's Staff
snippet:
Man-grub's Staff -  Dark Souls III - weapon - availability 
 availability : Reward for reaching Rank 2 in the Rosaria's Fingers covenant.

title: Man-grub's Staff
snippet:
Man-grub's Staff -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Man-grub's Staff is a very unique staff, in that its scaling attribute is not Intelligence, but Luck. As such, it requires a similarly unique build to utilize, as players must increase Intelligence to meet the casting requirements of various Sorceries, as well as Luck to boost the effectiveness of the catalyst itself.

The most effective way to use this staff is not to level Intelligence and Luck equally, but rather to level Intelligence and Attunement as supplements to a primarily Luck-based build. This gives the player access to powerful utility spells that complement Luck-based weapons, particularly in invasions, without the need to invest massive amounts of Intelligence to boost the hitting power of their spells.

title: Man-grub's Staff
snippet:
Man-grub's Staff -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : The **Man-grub's Staff** is a staff in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Man-grub's Staff
snippet:
Man-grub's Staff -  Dark Souls III - weapon - upgrades 
 upgrades : Reinforced with Titanite.

title: Man-grub's Staff
snippet:
At 40 Luck, the Man-grub's Staff has a higher effective Spell Buff than any other staff at 45 Intelligence, and only loses out to pure Intelligence-focused staves at 50 Intelligence and higher.

At the base wielding requirement of 18 Intelligence, players will have access to utility spells such as Chameleon, Snap Freeze, Great Heavy Soul Arrow and Spook. However, increasing Intelligence to 23 (which can also be achieved by simply equipping a Scholar Ring) will give the player access to relatively powerful spells such as Great Farron Dart, Farron Flashsword, Homing Soulmass, and Soul Greatsword.

title: Man-grub's Staff
snippet:
Man-grub's Staff -  Dark Souls III - weapon - notes 
 notes : The Spell Buff is always displayed at 100, but it does in fact increase with higher investments of Luck.
However, weapon buffs such as Great Magic Weapon will use the listed 100 Spell Buff.

title: Pyromancer (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Hand Axe is a surprisingly useful weapon. While it is pretty short, really only outranging Daggers and the Thrall Axe, it is quick and deals decent damage for its size. Its Weapon Art is Warcry, boosting weapon damage by 10% for 30 seconds and changing the heavy attack into a charge. While the charge is rather difficult to use for a Pyromancer in its default armor due to low Poise and the small size of the weapon itself, the damage boost is easy to use for foes resistant to Fire.

A mediocre Caduceus Round Shield rounds out the equipment setup. While it is unsuitable for blocking anything but the occasional Magic attack, it is still a light Parry tool. Actually blocking attacks should be left to the physically sturdy shields such as the Silver Eagle Kite Shield.

Its Pyromancer Set has good elemental defences and Poison and Curse resistances but bad physical defences.

The primary Pyromancy trainer is found early on, in the Undead Settlement.

title: Pyromancer (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Pyromancer (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Pyromancer** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a class with high Intelligence and Faith, making it suitable for builds based on Pyromancy or Dark Spells. It has the lowest Luck of all classes, a trait shared with the Knight.

Fireball is a strong spell and benefits from the fact that many early enemies are vulnerable to Fire, if a bit expensive and hard to aim due to it being thrown in an arc. The **Pyromancer** effectively still has two Pyromancies due to its casting tool, the Pyromancy Flame, having the classic pyromancy Combustion as its Weapon Art for a melee range alternative. The Great Swamp Ring will boost the damage of Fireball by 12% but since Combustion is a Weapon Art it won't be boosted.

title: Pyromancer (Dark Souls III)
snippet: Speaking of, the Pyromancy Flame will be the only casting tool for Pyromancy for a while and while it scales with both Intelligence and Faith it still works relatively well with more investment in one stat over the other. There is however one complicating factor for the scaling: unless Intelligence is at least 22 (goes down to a minimum of 18 as the Pyromancy Flame is upgraded), certain spells (Fireball, Fire Orb, and Great Chaos Fire Orb) won't scale with the Faith part of the Flame and therefore end up doing greatly decreased damage on a Faith build with insufficient investment in Intelligence. When wielded in the right hand it has the peculiar function of working as a free, short range punch that deals fire damage, helping against enemies weak to fire like the ooze-like Writhing Rotten Flesh in the Cathedral of the Deep.

title: Skeleton (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Skeleton (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Skeletons often appear in packs and their aggressive fighting style can easily kill an unprepared player. They use a variety of sword attacks, including a leaping slice, dashing lunge, and a dive attack that briefly causes them to fall apart. All of their attacks cause Bleed build-up, and can also parry and riposte the player for heavy damage.

Most skeletons reanimate when the player is close to them; this process takes a few seconds, however, leaving them vulnerable whilst they assemble themselves. They make a distinct sound when reanimating, so the player should listen out for it when exploring skeleton-inhabited lairs to avoid being ambushed. They are very weak to fire and will flail helplessly if ignited.

title: Skeleton (Dark Souls III)
snippet:

 notes : The unique rooted skeletons in the Undead Settlement's sewers are immune to Bleed, Poison, and Frost.
All variants can be parried, riposted and backstabbed (even the archers, when approached, will attempt to stab the player with their arrow which can be parried).

title: Skeleton (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Skeleton (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - enemy - description 
 description : Skeletons are piles of bones that reanimate when disturbed. Despite their brittle appearance, they are fast and aggressive opponents that can easily overwhelm an unwary player. They wield of variety of weapons and are capable of fighting despite missing limbs and even their heads.

Some skeletons in the Undead Settlement appear much more decayed, with plantlife growing out from their bodies.

 lead : **Skeletons** are enemies in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Skeleton (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Some of the skeletons in the Catacombs of Carthus have white glowing eyes and will reanimate a second time when defeated. The player should pay attention to see if they drop an item or souls; if they don't, then they will reanimate after a few seconds.

The player should not be overconfident when approaching a pile of bones, as they may randomly reassemble instantly and start attacking in quick succession.

Two non-hostile, hooded skeletons are found in the Catacombs of Carthus and will flee when approached. Each controls one of the big skeletal boulders that are rolling in their vicinity. Killing them will make the boulder to crash and break apart, revealing its contents.

title: Thief (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Though it has decent physical defence and dark defence for light armor, thanks to its Thief Mask and partial Deserter Set not covering its hands slot the **Thief** effectively has a flat defence penalty, since filling an armor slot gives a small bonus to flat defence. This is most easily fixed by taking the Master's Gloves from the Sword Master outside of Firelink Shrine, or by buying the Leather Gloves from the Shrine Handmaid.

It's more of a hard to use class, owing to its short and fairly weak weapon, asking for greater skill in dodging attacks to get close.

title: Thief (Dark Souls III)
snippet: Of the other two pieces of equipment, the Iron Round Shield is a small shield with a decent amount of physical defence (if not elemental defence) and a fairly high amount of Stability, along with a Small Shields improved Parry Weapon Art. The Short Bow on the other hand, is a fairly weak weapon with decent range (if a bit short for a Bow) that is best used for pulling foes from their starting location or to whittle down strong foes from just outside of their reach, instead of as a main weapon. As a light bow it has the advantageous quality of being able to fire directly out of a roll or sprint, and its Weapon Art, Rapid Fire, lets it potentially Poison easier with Poison Arrows. The starting Wood Arrows can be resupplied from the Shrine Handmaid, and will most likely have to be so fairly often if used for attacking since they have low damage.

title: Thief (Dark Souls III)
snippet: The Bandit's Knife has low damage per attack but can mostly make up for this against enemies that can be afflicted with Bleed, since the dagger's rapid attacks can proc the status effect quickly (even more so with a Carthus Rouge on it), and its Quickstep will let it maneuver quickly around foes or in areas that slow movement such as the swamp in Farron Keep. Otherwise, a flat attack buff such as Charcoal Pine Resin or Magic Weapon will help the most in increasing damage dealt.

title: Thief (Dark Souls III)

Thief (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Thief** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a class focused on Dexterity and Luck, making it good for a build focused on light or status inflicting weapons, such as the Scimitar or the Uchigatana, or weapons with the Sharp, Blood, or Hollow Infusions. It also has just enough Attunement and Intelligence to immediately use supportive Sorceries such as Spook for increased stealth or Magic Weapon for extra damage without additional investment in those stats.

title: Hollow
snippet:
Hollow -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Hollowing works somewhat differently in *Dark Souls III* compared to the previous games.
#Hollowing does not occur until the Ashen One has acquired at least one Dark Sigil. Every time the player dies, their "Hollowing" stat will increase by an amount equal to the number of Dark Sigils in their inventory. The Ashen One's body will start decaying after reaching a certain level of hollowing, but this effect is purely aesthetic.
#Hollowing has no negative effects on gameplay. However, it is required for certain NPC questlines and provides a bonus to luck when wielding Hollow weapons, if the player's hollowing level is at least 15.
#Unlike the previous installments, Hollowing and the "Host of Embers" status are unrelated; online interactions are governed only by the latter, meaning that hollowing does not affect invasions or summons.
#Hollowing can be reversed temporarily or permanently through two mechanics:

title: Infusion (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Infusion (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Infusion** is a gameplay mechanic in *Dark Souls III*. It is a form of weapon reinforcement. Infusing a weapon can be performed by talking with Blacksmith Andre and change the attributes of a weapon. For example, infusing a Scimitar with the Blessed infusion increases the scaling on that weapon for Faith, while reducing scaling for every other parameter.

title: Bleed (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bleed (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - infusion 
 infusion : Steady Hand McDuff can infuse most weapons with Bleed through the use of a Bleed Stone. Once a weapon is infused, the Bleed icon () will be displayed next to its image in the HUD.

Uninfused weapons imbued with Bleed gain a fixed Bleed buildup value (which does **not** scale with the Bleed Attack Bonus), but the base physical damage is lowered by 30%. For example, if a regular weapon that deals 100 physical damage is infused with Bleed, its stats switch over to 70 physical damage and 112 Bleed buildup.
Weapons with innate Bleed buildup gain an additional increase to Bleed buildup, but the base physical damage is lowered by 5%, as is the current scaling. For example, the Bandit's Knife goes from 65 physical damage + 67 Bleed buildup to 62 physical damage + 96 Bleed buildup when infused.
Shields gain additional Bleed resistance while lowering other resistances.

title: Hollow
snippet:
Hollow -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Hollowing in *Dark Souls II* is similar to the previous game, with a few key differences:

#Being hollow does not prevent being invaded by NPCs and other players.
#Each death suffered will reduce the player's max HP in increments of 5%. This will continue until it caps at 50% of maximum HP, unless the player has a sin level of wretch, which will cap it at 5%. With the Ring of Binding equipped, the HP cap is halved.
#The player's appearance visually degrades with each death.

Reverse Hollowing can be made instantly using a Human Effigy from the inventory. Alternatively, seeking Vendrick's blessing and wearing one of the four crowns will completely negate the effect of Hollowing, even upon death.

title: Hollow Assassin
snippet:
Hollow Assassin -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Hollow Assassins are very quick and agile, and have slightly more health than their fellow area hollows, so equipping a quick weapon is preferred in order to deal with them. They have very little poise, however, and simply raising up a shield will usually be enough for them to become staggered as they hit it, allowing for an easy kill.

It is not recommended to confront them in groups, as they can easily flank the player and combine a series of quick flurries, locking them in place until they die.

Namely, not being able to summon NPCs and other players in the form of white phantoms. Alternatively, being Hollow might also be desirable at times as it prevents the player from being invaded by other characters and players.

It is possible to "Reverse Hollowing" by offering Humanity at a bonfire; however, death results in reverting to a semi-Hollowed state. Also, the darksign can recreate the Chosen Undead's body in order to be reborn.

title: Hollow
snippet:
Hollow -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - causes 
 causes : The causes of Hollowing are not fully understood. Hollowing involves the loss of Humanity, the loss of purpose, or both.

Humanity seems to slow Hollowing. The characters closest to Hollowing do not drop any Humanity when killed. Using the Dark Hand, Humanity can be stolen from most characters, with the exception of several characters close to Hollowing (Crestfallen Warrior, Crestfallen Merchant, Undead Male Merchant, Undead Female Merchant). However, some fully Hollowed characters will drop large amounts of Humanity when killed, indicating that even Humanity cannot prevent Hollowing entirely.

title: Hollow
snippet:
Hollow -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - plot 
 plot : At the beginning of the Age of Fire, Gwyn marked the Dark Soul within every human being with a seal of fire, blocking its natural powers and causing humans to become mortal. As the First Flame began to fade, the Darksign's power consequently weakened and, as it was no longer able to adequately contain the Dark Soul, humans returned to being immortal, coming back to life with each death, and becoming known as Undead. However, humans are still marked by the Darksign, which consumes their Dark Soul as fuel to continue to exist. This leads the Undead to slowly lose their minds and become Hollows, as the strength that allows them to have a will and emotions and remain human is consumed from within them.

snippet:

 bleed_dark_souls_bleed : Bleed is a status effect that builds up after successive attacks from specific enemies' weapons. Once the bleed meter is full, it will deal damage based on a percentage of the victim's health. Taking too many bleed effects can become fatal very quickly. Bleed build-up can be stopped through use of a Bloodred Moss Clump, a Divine Blessing, or with the sorcery Remedy.

Bleed damage can be avoided by rolling the moment when the bleed meter fills.

title: Bleed (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Bleed (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - item - notes 
 notes : Bleed damage can be avoided by rolling the moment when the Bleed meter fills.
The bleed bar build-up per strike is not listed in the in-game weapon statistics, only the percentage of health lost when blood loss occurs.
Bleed damage is capped lower for damage against bosses.
The skeletons are able to inflict bleed upon the player when using their Scimitars and Falchions, despite these weapons not having a bleed effect when used by the player against enemies. Similarly, the Painting Guardians cannot use their weapons to inflict bleed upon the player, though the Painting Guardian Sword does inflict bleed upon enemies when wielded by the player.
Bleed damage is not blocked by any shields to any degree if the build-up was caused by an opponent in PvP. The same is true with Poison and Toxic.

The flat damage inflicted upon a successful Blood Loss proc alongside the percentage value varies depending on the source:

Saint Bident -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : This spear caters towards Faith-oriented builds, working either being infused with a Lightning Gem or buffed with resins or spells, such as Lightning Blade. Oddly enough, the Heavy infusion seems to be the only non-elemental infusion to benefit this spear. It is also one of the longest in its class, save for the Gargoyle Flame Spear and similar in length to the Lothric Knight Long Spear, which is a pike.

title: Scythe of the Forlorn
snippet:
Scythe of the Forlorn -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : While the Scythe of the Forlorn has decent normal stat scaling, it also scales with hollowing; that is, the more hollow the user is, the higher this scaling. Being in human form causes this weapon to scale *negatively* in this regard.

Special Scaling Explanations can be found in Attack Rating.

Infusing Bleed onto this weapon will reduce its stat scaling, but its Bleed effect will be increased and its Bleed damage doubled, causing this weapon at Bleed +5 to have one of the highest Bleed damages in the game. It should also be noted that infusing this weapon with Bleed will still cause it to have a higher Dark scaling if it were instead infused with Dark.

Infusing this weapon with Raw will reduce the negative scaling of being human.

title: Blacksteel Katana
snippet:
Blacksteel Katana -  Dark Souls II - weapon - notes 
 notes : When used by the Alonne Knights, the Blacksteel Katana causes bleed build-up. However, the variant available to the player has no bleed effect prior to infusion. Similarly the Captains have a lightning-infused version, and the player-obtainable version has no lightning element without infusion.
Ironically, it boasts a slightly-higher bleed effect reduction than most other katanas do, despite not being able to inflict bleed damage when wielded by the player.
The 2H heavy attacks can be performed faster after Rolling and Backstep attacks, as well as after guard breaks and a single 2H light attack. This can make the Blacksteel Katana perform combos easily.

title: Vitality (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Vitality (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Vitality** is one of the eight base stats in *Dark Souls* that can be increased when leveling up. Investing in vitality increases the player's maximum health points (HP).

Contrary to the vitality stats in *Dark Souls II* and *Dark Souls III*, vitality in *Dark Souls* does not affect the player's maximum equipment load. In *Dark Souls*, equipment load is governed by endurance.

title: Pharis
snippet:
More supporting evidence is found within *Dark Souls II*, which ties the equipment of Pharis to a legendary female archer, as well as in *Dark Souls III*, in which Pharis's equipment is yet again found in a location associated with the Forest Hunter Archer, that being Farron Keep, a forested swamp that is heavily implied to be what became of Darkroot Garden in the future. The description of the hat from that game also states that it is especially favored by forest hunters, which is yet another point of connection with the Forest Hunter Archer.

Some members of the *Dark Souls* community have assumed that the two characters can't be the same due to Pharis being described with male pronouns, and the Forest Hunter Archer being a woman. However, the Japanese version does not make any clear statement on Pharis's gender, and the hat's design has been retconned to be unisex in both *Dark Souls II* and *Dark Souls III*.
